item.title: P\'osa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $\gamma>0$, there exists $C=C(k,\gamma)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying \[ g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+\gamma\right) \binom{n-1}{k-1}p \qquad(1\le i<n/2) \] contains a Hamilton Berge cycle. The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic P\'osa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zhang, Ailian Chen, Qinghai Liu

item.title: Upper bound on the size of subgraphs avoiding cycles of girth length in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-free if it contains no copy of $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Although $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$ has been extensively studied for various specific graphs $G$, such as hypercubes, complete transposition graphs, and doubled Johnson graphs, very few results are known for general graphs. For a graph $G$ of girth $g$, let $C_{g}$ denote the cycle of length $g$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, C_{g})$ for graphs $G$ in which every edge is contained in a fixed number of $g$-cycles, and establish a general upper bound on it. This bound generalizes the classical results on hypercubes and provides a unified approach for general graphs. Furthermore, we apply this bound to derive explicit upper bounds for several specific graphs, including $K_{n,n,\ldots,n}$, $K_{n}\times K_{n}$, $C_{m}\times C_{n}$, $S_{n}$, $AG_{n}$, $CT_{n}$ and $J(n;k,k+1)$.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Li Zhao, Yu-Qi Li

item.title: Algorithms for Short Human-Verifiable Proofs of Non-Word-Representability
item.description: arXiv:2611.08553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is word-representable if it can be represented using alternation of letters in words. The class of word-representable graphs generalizes several important graph families and admits a characterization via semi-transitive orientations. Recognizing word-representability is an NP-complete problem, and a major bottleneck in the theory of word-representable graphs is providing efficient justifications of non-word-representability of graphs, rather than merely referring to software verification. Recently, Kitaev and Sun initiated the development of methods for the automatic generation of human-verifiable proofs of non-word-representability. They introduced three algorithms and evaluated their performance on the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices, which constitute a fairly small sample set. In this paper, we confirm their ranking of the algorithms by testing them on all non-word-representable graphs on eight and nine vertices. We further introduce three new algorithms, one of which significantly outperforms the previously best method on graphs with at most nine vertices, producing substantially shorter proofs. We apply this algorithm to shorten a known proof of non-word-representability of the Shrikhande graph and to produce a proof of non-word-representability of a certain subgraph of the Kneser graph $K(8,3)$. This subgraph is the first known example of a triangle-free non-word-representable graph, presented in the literature with reference only to a computational proof. As a by-product of our study, we correct an error in the repeatedly published list of the 25 connected non-word-representable graphs on seven vertices.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Kitaev, Junting Zhong

item.title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$. For these codes the stable profile is equivalent to minimality with the largest possible minimum distance; for even $m$ the analogous class consists of minimal MRD codes. More generally, for $1\le\tau\le m-2$ and $\gcd(m,\tau+1)=1$, we obtain nondegenerate $\tau$-minimal codes of length $(\tau+1)K$ for every sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $q$. We also construct maximum $h$-designs whose number of members grows exponentially with the ambient dimension at fixed $q,n,h$, and the associated maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes with a growing number of equal long blocks. In extension degree five, the ordinary and $2$-minimal constructions hold for every $q$ and every $K\ge32$ and $K\ge59$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Giannoni

item.title: Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers
item.description: arXiv:2611.08674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration. A classical rooted-forest enumeration leads in both problems to $\mathcal T(x)$, the exponential generating function for rooted labeled trees. For $f=g\circ f\circ g$, the values on the cycles of $g$ determine all remaining values. The exponential generating function $\mathcal D$ for these ordered pairs and the ordinary generating function $\mathcal A$ for endofunctions up to relabeling satisfy $\mathcal D(x)=\mathcal A(\mathcal T(x))$. Finally, we count functions on $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ satisfying $f(ax)=af(x)$, first for prime multipliers $a$ and then for a broader class of composite multipliers. In each problem, fixing one map exposes independent choices for the other through its functional digraph or its fibers.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.08819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$. In fact, rather surprisingly, in sufficiently large dimensions $d$ the number of vertices (equivalently, by duality, the number of facets) can be as large as theoretically possible, namely doubly exponential in $d$. These results were found using GPT-6.1 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Hofscheier, Benjamin Nill

item.title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.08862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $\chi_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $\chi_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts. The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.
item.dc:creator: Reza Naserasr

item.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
item.description: arXiv:2611.09000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Exoo, Theodore Kolokolnikov

item.title: Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $\pi/2+\delta$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $\delta>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $\pi/2+\delta$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenkun Li, Jinmin Wang, Jing Yu

item.title: Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.
item.dc:creator: Lihua Wei, Kexiang Xu

item.title: Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs. The former is characterized by ear decompositions. For the latter, we first characterize the $3$-connected case using the theory of line graphs and then extend the characterization to the general case by a suitable $2$-sum operation.
item.dc:creator: Huaibin Zhou, Mingyang Guo, Xiumei Wang

item.title: Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas
item.description: arXiv:2611.09076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes. We determine exact eventual formulas when the fixed set has six, seven or eight items. The eight-item formula has a period-three correction. We explain this correction by optimizing the sizes of shared test pieces within fixed decision-tree prefixes. For each fixed finite family of such prefixes ending in star forests, the optimal deficit is eventually a rational polynomial plus a bounded periodic function. The asymptotic proofs are analytic; the exact formulas also use integer constructions and rational exclusion certificates.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Karpelevitch

item.title: The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2611.09111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$. The construction combines faithful stress-free Gram representations, a one-coordinate lift for each excess core edge, exact orthogonal-frame completion, and a Stiefel-manifold pendant-extension argument.
item.dc:creator: Binh T. Nguyen

item.title: Every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most 6
item.description: arXiv:2611.09125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most $6$. Weak-strict degeneracy is the weak degeneracy of Bernshteyn and Lee plus one, so it bounds the coloring parameters controlled by weak degeneracy. In particular, every IC-planar graph is $6$-choosable, $6$-DP-colorable and $6$-paintable, which strengthens the theorem of Yang, Wang, Wang and Lih that IC-planar graphs are $6$-choosable. An IC-planar graph is a subgraph of a plane graph in which a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint inner $4$-faces, called marked faces, receive both diagonals. Our main tool is a Thomassen-type statement for such graphs: vertices of marked faces get one extra unit, except those in a prescribed independent set of boundary vertices. With no marked faces, this statement is exactly the theorem of Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge that gives weak-strict degeneracy at most $5$ for planar graphs, so it contains both results. We prove it by a minimal-counterexample argument following Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge. The new ingredients are a deletion rule that turns destroyed marked faces into ordinary edges, a pseudo-$2$-chord lemma for paths that use one diagonal, and a choice of orientation of the outer cycle that avoids a vertex of the independent set joined to two vertices of the prescribed boundary path.
item.dc:creator: Zhen He, Yilong Li, Tao Wang, Xiaojing Yang

item.title: A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.09347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_2}\). We rigorously prove its Petersen-free property, thereby improving the previously documented lower bound to \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}) \ge 21\). Furthermore, we demonstrate the limit of this structural family by showing that the natural extension \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_3}\) contains a Petersen subgraph.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Si

item.title: On the Motzkin-Straus theorem and clique number for k-uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a Motzkin-Straus type equality for k-uniform hypergraphs under certain conditions, which extends the classical Motzkin--Straus theorem for graphs. Using this equality, we present several spectral bounds for the clique number of k-uniform hypergraphs in terms of the spectral radii of the adjacency, signless Laplacian, and Laplacian tensors. When k=2, the bounds coincide with the corresponding known results for graphs.
item.dc:creator: Chunli Deng, Shaohuan Hao, Haifeng Li

item.title: A 4-regular graph with 4/5 of its vertices satisfying the \v{S}olt\'es property
item.description: arXiv:2611.09416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of its vertices. A vertex $v$ is called a \v{S}olt\'es vertex if $G-v$ is connected and $W(G-v)=W(G)$. Since the cycle $C_{11}$ is the only known graph in which every vertex is a \v{S}olt\'es vertex, a natural problem is to construct other graphs with as large a proportion of such vertices as possible. We construct a $4$-regular graph with \v{S}olt\'es fraction $4/5$, improving the previous value of $2/3$.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Dobrynin

item.title: Mutual-visibility in (d, 5)-graphs with excess
item.description: arXiv:2611.09513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The author investigates mutual visibility in regular graphs of girth at least 5, with particular emphasis on graphs with excess. A general upper bound on the mutual-visibility number is established in terms of the degree and order. More significantly, an algebraic inequality is derived that restricts the mutual-visibility number of $(d,5,+\delta)$-graphs. As applications, the mutual-visibility number of the Robertson graph is shown to be 9, and upper bounds are obtained for the $(5,5)$-cages and the $(6,5)$-cage.
item.dc:creator: Tonny K. B

item.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.
item.dc:creator: Jane Ivy Coons, Ben Hollering, Niharika Chakrabarty Paul

item.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane developed by Haiman.
item.dc:creator: Peter L. Guo, Mingyang Kang, Changjian Su, Rui Xiong

item.title: The maximum size of $3$-distance binary codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that for every positive integer $n \ge 24$, the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of vectors from $\{-1,1\}^n$ with at most three distinct Hamming distances is equal to $\binom{n}{3}+n$. The threshold $n=24$ is best possible.
item.dc:creator: Valjakas Djaljapayan, Hao Huang, Wei-Hsuan Yu

item.title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$. The resulting score has mean $(3/2)^d$ for every partition, while its distribution reflects the geometry of the tiling. Comparing two such scores, with the shifts chosen independently, defines a game in which the larger score wins. In dimension $d=4$, we construct a geometric realization of the Steinhaus--Trybu{\l}a paradox: three periodic partitions form a cycle in which each beats the next with probability strictly greater than $1/2$. We describe local configurations by finite cube tiling codes and prove that every resulting list of counts is majorized by that of the simple code $C_d=\{0,2\}^d$. Nevertheless, every non-simple code differing from $C_d$ in only two coordinate directions beats it, with a sharp lower bound on the winning margin. We also show that the ratio of wins to losses of $C_d$ has limit superior at most $1$ as the dimension tends to infinity, uniformly over opposing codes. For $4\mathbb{Z}^d$-periodic tilings, changing the window size can repeatedly reverse the winner, but the winning margin eventually stabilizes separately for side lengths $4m+1$ and $4m+3$.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej P. Kisielewicz

item.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.
item.dc:creator: Gautam K. Das, Kamal Santra

item.title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.08653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_\alpha f>\lambda\}\bigr) \lesssim_{\alpha,s} \frac1\lambda\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{\alpha,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-R\'ios and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{r\alpha}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{r\alpha}$ and $k^{r(1-\alpha)}$. We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<\alpha<1$. In the subcritical range $0<\alpha<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_\alpha$. We also prove that $M_\alpha w\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\le\alpha<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_\alpha w\lesssim w$.
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Iba\~nez-Firnkorn, Jorgelina Recchi

item.title: Levenshtein-type bounds for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal $s$-codes and for minimal energy) for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid $(a,b)$. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials). Under these hypotheses and suitable node-location assumptions, the resulting cardinality bounds are optimal within the corresponding degree restriction and unique under natural nondegeneracy conditions. Under proper conditions on the quadrature nodes, we obtain universal lower energy bounds by utilizing Hermite interpolants as polynomial solutions of the respective linear program. Common test functions characterize optimality in the full polynomial linear programs under mild additional assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Peter Dragnev, Peter Grabner

item.title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $\pi$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Bose, Bobby Miraftab, Tyler Tuttle

item.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
item.dc:creator: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov

item.title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
item.description: arXiv:2611.09215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\ll\eta\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.
item.dc:creator: Jaehun Lee

item.title: Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $\Gamma$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, and Szegedy. As applications of our dynamical results, we obtain the following combinatorial theorems. Let $A\subseteq \Gamma$ be a set of positive upper Banach density. Then there are infinite sets $B_1,\ldots, B_k\subseteq \Gamma$ such that $B_1+\dots+B_k\subseteq A$. If $\Gamma$ satisfies a necessary divisibility assumption, then there are also $t\in \Gamma$ and an infinite set $B\subseteq \Gamma$ such that $A-t$ contains the set of all sums of $m$ pairwise distinct elements of $B$ for all $m\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. For arbitrary $k$, these density finite sums theorems were only known in the integers previously.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Ackelsberg, Asgar Jamneshan, Or Shalom

item.title: Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.09415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations. We prove that, under these bounds, an intersection of $T$-ideals is contained in such a product only if one member is. This proves Berele's Conjecture~3 and, consequently, his Conjecture~1 \cite{Berele2012}. We also characterize inclusions between ordered products by an explicit combinatorial criterion, proving his Conjecture~2 and answering his Question~2 \cite{Berele2012}. These results characterize inclusions between arbitrary intersections of products of nonzero proper verbally prime $T$-ideals and show that every nonzero such intersection has a unique finite irredundant representation. As an application, we characterize finite quivers whose path algebras have the same polynomial identities as some, equivalently every, positive power of their arrow ideals.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: New persistent chain spaces: identifying and computing the relevant persistent Laplacians of a filtration
item.description: arXiv:2611.09610v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space. We show that the new persistent chain spaces of all earlier pairs form a direct sum decomposition of this space, so that every persistent up-Laplacian in the filtration is determined by them. Moreover, the new persistent chain spaces are non-trivial only at pairs given by the persistence pairing in the same and in the next homological dimension, so that the persistence pairing determines exactly where the persistent up-Laplacian can change. Experiments on several types of point clouds show that evaluating persistent Laplacians only at these pairs reduces the computation time, both for our implementation and for existing software.
item.dc:creator: Joris Kirchner, Martina Vittorietti

item.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
item.description: arXiv:2611.09627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor. We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.
item.dc:creator: Jadwiga Czy\.zewska, Tom\'a\v{s} Masa\v{r}\'ik, Marcin Pilipczuk, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski

item.title: Matroid products via submodular coupling
item.description: arXiv:2411.02197v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of matroid products traces back to the 1970s, when Lov\'asz and Mason studied the existence of various types of matroid products with different strengths. Among these, the tensor product is arguably the most important, which can be considered as an extension of the tensor product from linear algebra. However, Las Vergnas showed that the tensor product of two matroids does not always exist. Over the following four decades, matroid products remained surprisingly underexplored, regaining attention only in recent years due to applications in tropical geometry and the limit theory of matroids. In this paper, inspired by the concept of coupling in probability theory, we introduce the notion of coupling for matroids -- or, more generally, for submodular set functions. This operation can be viewed as a relaxation of the tensor product. Unlike the tensor product, however, we prove that a coupling always exists for any two submodular functions and can be chosen to be increasing if the original functions are increasing. As a corollary, we show that two matroids always admit a matroid coupling, leading to a novel operation on matroids. Our construction is algorithmic, providing an oracle for the coupling matroid through a polynomial number of oracle calls to the original matroids. We apply this construction to derive new necessary conditions for matroid representability and establish connection between tensor products and Ingleton's inequality. Additionally, we verify the existence of set functions that are universal with respect to a given property, meaning any set function over a finite domain with that property can be obtained as a quotient.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: K. B\'erczi, B. Geh\'er, A. Imolay, L. Lov\'asz, B. Maga, T. Schwarcz: Matroid products via submodular coupling, Advances in Combinatorics, 2026:11
item.dc:creator: Krist\'of B\'erczi, Bogl\'arka Geh\'er, Andr\'as Imolay, L\'aszl\'o Lov\'asz, Bal\'azs Maga, Tam\'as Schwarcz

item.title: Three-Neighbour Bootstrap Percolation in Thin Three-Dimensional Grids
item.description: arXiv:2509.13589v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the status of the problem of determining minimum-sized percolating sets in $a \times b \times c$ grids under the $3$-neighbour process. Using several new constructions, we show that optimal percolating sets exist whenever $\min(a,b,c) \ge 7$. As an important step toward this, we also show that all grids with $\min(a,b,c) \ge 4$ have a percolating set whose size exactly achieves the lower bound $(ab+ac+bc)/3$ whenever this value is an integer.
item.dc:creator: Will Dolphin, Peter J. Dukes

item.title: An Expander Mixing Lemma for Directed Graphs via Transition Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2511.01738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an Expander Mixing Lemma for directed graphs in terms of the eigenvalues of a transition matrix, extending the classical spectral inequality to the non-symmetric setting. This formulation works with the complex spectrum of the transition matrix and incorporates the conditioning of its eigenbasis through a condition number. For connected, non-bipartite, undirected regular graphs, the result reduces to the classical Expander Mixing Lemma. More generally, the theorem provides a framework for studying structural properties of directed graphs through the spectra of non-normal matrices.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Carter

item.title: Absolute incidence theorems and tilings
item.description: arXiv:2512.14316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a precise definition of incidence theorems in plane projective geometry and introduce the notion of absolute incidence theorems, which hold over any ring. Fomin and Pylyavskyy describe how to obtain incidence theorems from tilings of an orientable surface; they call this result the master theorem. Instances of the master theorem are always absolute incidence theorems. As most classically known incidence theorems are instances of the master theorem, they are absolute incidence theorems. We give an explicit example of an incidence theorem involving 13 points that is not an absolute incidence theorem, and therefore is not an instance of the master theorem.
item.dc:creator: Lukas K\"uhne, Matt Larson

item.title: Cyclic sieving phenomena for trees and tree-rooted maps
item.description: arXiv:2512.18656v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove cyclic sieving phenomena satisfied by corner-rooted plane trees (alias ordered trees). The sets of rooted plane trees that we consider are: (1) all trees with $n$ nodes; (2) all trees with $n$ nodes and $k$ leaves; (3) all trees with a given degree distribution of the nodes. Moreover, we consider four different cyclic group actions: (1) the root is moved to the next corner along a tour of the tree; (2) only trees in which the root is at a leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next leaf; (3) only trees in which the root is at a non-leaf are considered, and the action moves the root to the next non-leaf corner; (4) only trees in which the root is at a node of degree $\delta$ are considered, for a fixed $\delta$, and the action moves the root to the next corner of this type. We prove a cyclic sieving phenomenon for each meaningful combination of these sets and actions. As a bonus, we also establish corresponding cyclic sieving phenomena for tree-rooted planar maps.
item.dc:creator: Mireille Bousquet-M\'elou, Christian Krattenthaler

item.title: Biregular bipartite multigraphs and matchings in tensor products of bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.18253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We answer a question of P. Higgins on permutations and involutions in binary arrays, arising in the study of regular finite semigroups. For a binary rectangular matrix M, we prove that if there is a permutation pi(x, y) = (f(x, y), g(x, y)) of its cells satisfying M(x, g(x,y)) = 1 for every cell, then there is an involution with the same property. The elementary proof places coins in the nonzero cells, reduces their support to a forest, and assigns consecutive integer weights to the coins incident to each row and column. We also prove a multiplicativity formula for bipartite expansion and a perfect matching theorem for tensor products of supports of matrices with prescribed margins. We study a stronger conjecture of F. Petrov on disjoint swaps in biregular bipartite multigraphs. We prove this conjecture for k = mn + eps, |eps| <= 2, and for n = 6, k = 6m + 3, and give a group-theoretic reformulation.
item.dc:creator: Ilya I. Bogdanov, Fedor Petrov, Anton Sadovnichiy, Fedor Ushakov

item.title: Inversion monotonicity in subclasses of the 1324-avoiders
item.description: arXiv:2604.01143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove injectively that the pattern-avoiding permutation classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 231)$ and $\mathrm{Av}(1324, 2314, 3214, 4213)$ are inversion monotone: for every $k$, the number of length-$n$ permutations with $k$ inversions in either class is weakly increasing in $n$. These are the first known nontrivial examples of the phenomenon. The latter is a special case of a general construction. We also characterize the finitely based permutation classes in which the number of length-$n$ members with a fixed number of inversions stabilizes as $n$ grows, and determine the limiting values for all classes $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ with $p \in S_4$. Connections to several nice families of integer partitions are revealed. Lastly, we show that for asymptotically almost every pattern $p \in \mathrm{Av}(1324)$, the class $\mathrm{Av}(1324, p)$ is inversion monotone in the region $n \geq \frac{k+7}{2}$, expanding on the work of Linusson and Verkama. This work is motivated by the conjectures of Claesson, Jel\'inek and Steingr\'imsson that $\mathrm{Av}(1324)$, and more generally $\mathrm{Av}(p)$ for every nonidentity pattern $p$, is inversion monotone.
item.dc:creator: Anders Claesson, Svante Linusson, Henning Ulfarsson, Emil Verkama

item.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
item.description: arXiv:2605.02254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between distinct vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya, Xiwang Cao

item.title: On Congruences modulo powers of 3 for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partitions in $k$-Colors
item.dc:creator: Anjelin Mariya Johnson, S. N. Fathima

item.title: Mersenne Representation, the Conolly Sequence, and Soliton Profiles over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.22202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers \(2^{k}-1\), and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side. We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect. Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo \(3\) yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.
item.dc:creator: Fumitaka Yura

item.title: Nearly balanced spanning subdivisions in dense digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.14432v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pavez-Sign\'e [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128] conjectured a Dirac-type condition for spanning $H$-subdivisions and asked whether the subdivision paths can additionally be required to have similar lengths. Lee [European J. Combin. 124 (2025), 104059] resolved the existence conjecture in the stronger setting of digraphs. We answer the length-control question in this stronger directed setting: for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $C_0>0$ such that, for every digraph $H$ with $h$ arcs and no isolated vertices, every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ with $n\ge C_0h$ and $\delta^0(D)\ge(1/2+\varepsilon)n$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision whose subdivision paths have lengths differing by at most one.
item.dc:creator: Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei

item.title: Spanning $H$-subdivisions with Prescribed Path Lengths
item.description: arXiv:2608.15786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study spanning $H$-subdivisions in dense graphs where the length of every subdivision path is prescribed in advance. This problem is motivated in part by a question of Pavez-Sign\'e [Combin. Probab. Comput. 33 (2024), 121--128], who asked whether the subdivision paths in a spanning $H$-subdivision can be required to have similar lengths. Let $h\ge3$ be an integer and let $0<\beta\ll\alpha\ll1/h$. We prove that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\ge n/2+\lfloor h/3\rfloor$ has the following property. For every graph $H$ with $h$ edges and no isolated vertices, write $E(H)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_h\}$, and every choice of integers $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_h\ge4$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^h\ell_i=n-|V(H)|+h$ and $\sum_{\ell_i<\alpha n}\ell_i\le\beta n$, the graph $G$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision in which the $i$th edge of $H$ is replaced by a path of length exactly $\ell_i$. We also give a family of examples showing that a linear additive term in $h$ is necessary in general.
item.dc:creator: Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei

item.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2609.01866v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs. A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Gerling

item.title: Fixed-Perimeter Franklin Statistics and an Eventual Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2609.12005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gray, Payne, Swisher, and Watson conjectured that, for fixed integers $j \geq 0$ and $k \geq 2$, the number $FD_{j,k}(n)$ of partitions of perimeter $n$ having exactly $j$ part sizes of multiplicity at least $k$ is eventually at least the number $FO_{j,k}(n)$ having exactly $j$ distinct occurring part sizes divisible by $k$. We derive bivariate generating functions for both statistics using the profile-word encoding of a partition. For $k \geq 3$, coefficient extraction shows that fixing $j$ changes the order of the dominant pole but not its location. The corresponding dominant singularities are positive real numbers $\rho_k$ and $\sigma_k$, where $\rho_k$ satisfies $\rho_k+\rho_k^2+\cdots+\rho_k^k=1$ and $\sigma_k$ satisfies $\sigma_k^k=(1-\sigma_k)^{k-1}$. We prove that $\rho_k<\sigma_k$ for every $k \geq 3$. Consequently, $FD_{j,k}(n)/FO_{j,k}(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, proving the conjecture and yielding a strict eventual inequality for $k \geq 3$. The case $k=2$ recovers the known exact identity.
item.dc:creator: Marcus McCrea

item.title: Aigner's majorization conjecture in quantitative group testing: counterexamples and eventual sufficiency for star forests
item.description: arXiv:2609.38284v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We refute Aigner's majorization conjecture for star forests in adaptive quantitative group testing with two defective items. Each test counts the defectives in a chosen subset; the possible defective pairs form the edges of a star forest. Aigner's necessary majorization condition is sufficient through five tests but is not sufficient at any budget from six onward. Nevertheless, for every fixed number of stars, it becomes sufficient once the test budget is large enough. We prove that majorization is sufficient for all forests with at most twenty-nine stars, and that this bound is sharp. We also construct counterexamples that pass arbitrarily many successive compatibility checks based on majorization. The five-test converse, counterexamples, eventual sufficiency theorem and unbounded-delay construction have analytic proofs. The sharp finite support bounds also use exact integer-inequality certificates.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Karpelevitch

item.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.25863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Togni

item.title: An upper bound of 60 for the Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
item.description: arXiv:2610.36648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 60. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.
item.dc:creator: Milos Tatarevic

item.title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.00720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one. Following the sharp result of Chen et al. [arXiv:2610.38574v1 (2026)] for at most one such vertex, we determine the exact digirth threshold when at most $r\ge4$ such vertices are permitted. Specifically, for all integers $k\ge2$ and $r\ge4$, every digraph of minimum out-degree at least one, with at most $r$ vertices of out-degree one and digirth at least $r(k-1)+1$, contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang, Panpan Cheng

item.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.01241v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Ganguly

item.title: Perfect 1-factorisations of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2611.01807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A perfect 1-factorisation (P1F) of $K_{2n}$ is a partition of its edges into $2n-1$ perfect matchings, any two of which form a Hamiltonian cycle. Exhaustive classification is known only up to $K_{16}$. We present a method for the exhaustive generation, up to isomorphism, of perfect 1-factorisations with a non-trivial automorphism group, which reduces the search tree far enough to make $K_{18}$ and beyond feasible. It combines two ideas. For automorphism groups of order greater than 2, classical results of Ihrig on the automorphisms of P1Fs are used as tools that reject almost all prescribed cycle types without search. For the order-2 case, which dominates, candidates are recalculated from inherited compatibility lists, in the spirit of Gill and Wanless, with an outer loop over two further rows that keeps those lists small, and Ihrig's results restrict the first factor. As the numerical proof of the method we compute all 10,710 P1Fs of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group; before, only six were known.
item.dc:creator: Andrei V. Ivanov, Leonid M. Tertitski

item.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03763v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every fixed odd $d\ge5$, we prove that the circular flow number of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph is asymptotically almost surely less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_d>0$. At degree five the upper bound is $3-1/24006$. At degree seven it is $21/8$, answering a question of Li and Li. For every fixed $p\ge1$, we also obtain a strongly connected Jaeger orientation at degree $4p+1$, with outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$. At large degrees we count dense bisections together with sets that violate their cut inequalities. This gives flow intervals of length $O(d^{-2})$ above the maximum-bisection lower bound of Li and Li. The finite-degree estimates, together with the large-degree transfer, also prove the conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis that the threshold for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the corresponding bisection threshold by at most one.
item.dc:creator: Amir Jafari

item.title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
item.description: arXiv:2611.05423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le\max\{\omega(G),\Delta(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Lizhong Chen

item.title: Line crossing problem for biased monotonic random walks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:0709.3316v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A $\beta$-biased monotonic random walk in the plane moves from $(x,y)$ to $(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y+1)$ with probabilities $1/(\beta+1)$ and $\beta/(\beta+1)$. We study $\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that the walk started at the origin ever visits a lattice point strictly above the line $y=\alpha x+d$, and $\Psi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that it visits a lattice point \emph{on} the line after leaving the origin. For integer slopes $\alpha=p$ we show $\Phi_\beta(p,d)=\rho^{\lfloor d\rfloor+1}$, where $\rho$ is the smallest positive root of $y^{p+1}-(\beta+1)y+\beta=0$, give the Fuss--Catalan series for $\rho$, identify $\rho$ with the extinction probability of a Galton--Watson process, and compute the exact law and mean of the first crossing point. We prove that the return probability is $\Psi_\beta(p,0)=(p+1)(1-\beta/((\beta+1)\rho))$, which equals $(p+1)/(\beta+1)$ for $\beta\ge p$. For rational slopes $\alpha=r/s$ we obtain $\Phi_\beta$ in closed form from the $s$ large roots of the kernel $\tfrac{\beta}{\beta+1}z^{r+s}-z^r+\tfrac1{\beta+1}$, and $\Psi_\beta$ as a ratio of Green's functions. For arbitrary real $\alpha$ we prove that the walk crosses every line $y=\alpha x+d$ almost surely if and only if $\beta\ge\alpha$, and we establish the two-sided bound $e^{-\theta(d+1)}\le\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)<e^{-\theta d}$ with an explicit Lundberg exponent $\theta$. Finally, $\alpha\mapsto\Phi_\beta(\alpha,0)$ is a pure jump function: it is constant on $[0,\beta]$, continuous at every irrational point and has a jump at every rational $\alpha>\beta$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2411.17572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Br\"and\'en and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Yupeng Li, Jacob P. Matherne

item.title: Traits and tangles: An analysis of the Big Five paradigm by tangle-based clustering
item.description: arXiv:2411.18670v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the recently developed mathematical theory of tangles, we re-assess the mathematical foundations for applications of the five factor model in personality tests by a new, mathematically rigorous, quantitative method. Our findings broadly confirm the validity of current tests, but also show that more detailed information can be extracted from existing data. We found that the big five traits appear at different levels of scrutiny. Some already emerge at a coarse resolution of our tools at which others cannot yet be discerned, while at a resolution where these _can_ be discerned, and distinguished, some of the former traits are no longer visible but have split into more refined traits or disintegrated altogether. We also identified traits other than the five targeted in those tests. These include more general traits combining two or more of the big five, as well as more specific traits refining some of them. All our analysis is structural and quantitative, and thus rigorous in explicitly defined mathematical terms. Since tangles, once computed, can be described concisely in terms of very few explicit statements referring only to the test questions used, our findings are also directly open to interpretation by experts in psychology. Tangle analysis can be applied similarly to other topics in psychology. Our paper is intended to serve as a first indication of what may be possible.
item.dc:creator: Hanno von Bergen, Reinhard Diestel

item.title: The symmetrized sum of finite $q$-multiple harmonic sums with one exceptional index
item.description: arXiv:2602.02480v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we give explicit expressions for $q$-harmonic sums on $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ indices. The case $A=1$ has been extensively studied, and a variety of identities, explicit evaluations, and structural properties are known. Likewise, numerous explicit evaluations are available for $q$-multiple zeta values and $q$-harmonic sums with uniform indices $A-\cdots-A$. Although several methods are available for treating non-uniform indices, explicit evaluations for the pattern $1-\cdots-1,A,1-\cdots-1$ remain comparatively scarce. The case $A=2$ was settled only recently. In this paper, we extend this framework to the general case $A\ge3$ as the total sum with the theory of the elementary symmetric functions, though we do not generally evaluate each summand at a prescribed position of $A$. We obtain explicit formulas in terms of binomial coefficients and degenerate Bernoulli numbers. Some expressions about $2-\cdots-2,A,2-\cdots-2$ are also shown.
item.dc:creator: Hideaki Ishikawa, Takao Komatsu

item.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2606.11987v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.
item.dc:creator: Ragnar Freij-Hollanti, Kirsten D. Morris, Patricija \v{S}apokait\.e

item.title: The maximum volume polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the sphere
item.description: arXiv:2608.04392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A classical problem in convex and discrete geometry asks for the convex polyhedron of greatest volume whose vertices are chosen from the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$. For a prescribed number $N$ of vertices, the problem is known only in a small number of cases, namely $4\leq N\leq 8$ and $N=12$. In the case $N=9$, Wimmer showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the volume maximizer must be combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. In this note, we complete the proof by determining the volume maximizer among all inscribed polytopes which are combinatorially equivalent to a triaugmented triangular prism. Consequently, every convex polyhedron with at most nine vertices on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has volume at most $3\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}-3}$, with equality, up to rotation, precisely for the ``symmetric'' triaugmented triangular prism whose vertex coordinates we compute exactly.
item.dc:creator: Steven Hoehner, Jeff Ledford

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: Betti Numbers of Odd Biisotropic Symplectic Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.03309v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the singular cohomology groups of odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ by presenting an explicit dimension-preserving combinatorial bijection between the Bialynicki-Birula cells in $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ and the Schubert cells in $\operatorname{Gr}(k, 2n+2-k)$.
item.dc:creator: Anton Fonarev, Alexander Kuznetsov
